canonical_statement: Let 0 < p < infinity and let (f_n) be measurable functions on a measure space such that f_n converges almost everywhere to f and the integrals of |f_n|^p are uniformly bounded. Then the integral of |f_n|^p minus the integral of |f_n-f|^p converges to the integral of |f|^p.
domain_and_universes: A measure space (X, Sigma, mu), real exponent p with 0 < p, and real- or complex-valued measurable functions f_n and f; exact Lean universes and scalar choice remain for the statement phase
conclusion: integral |f_n|^p dmu - integral |f_n-f|^p dmu -> integral |f|^p dmu
degenerate_cases: p = 0 and p < 0 are excluded. Infinite-valued integrals are excluded by the uniform finite bound. Finite versus sigma-finite measure is intentionally not strengthened at intake.

alternate_encodings.target: L^p norm splitting for 1 <= p < infinity
alternate_encodings.relationship: important restricted corollary, not a substitute for the canonical p > 0 integral theorem
candidate encoding of nonnegative power integrals
